[{"id": "BLNJD3muSe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc3Foundations Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "srY9IZhv07", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Foundations module holds what your church is and believes: the Church record with its name, address and settings, your statement of beliefs, and the weekly numbers of church life. It also explains how Churchit works when one organization has more than one church, how to send records to other systems, and how Churchit uses AI when your church turns it on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rSJvCZYPeW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Managers change the Church record and the beliefs. Other staff can read them. Some parts of this manual, such as AI and webhooks, are for a System Manager.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iK3FZ-208_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Foundations sidebar lists Churches, Beliefs and the Churches Report. The workspace shows the number of churches and beliefs and a chart of the beliefs added each month. The Settings sidebar starts with Church (the church name, address and image) and, for a System Manager, System Settings (time zone, currency and date format). The dock at the left hides a module when your roles give you no page in it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DAdlKmRMB3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u26eaChurches", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4LbqAeDguj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Church record holds your church's details: its name and abbreviation, address, phone and email, about text, mission statement, verse, image, and settings such as the default Bible translation. Churchit uses them on the website, the bulletin, the Church Directory, giving statements and emails. A new site starts with one church called My Church: open it and fill in your own details first. To see what each field means, click ..., then Take the Tour, on the Church form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UFBqjjJX_w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uEBRtv2l60", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Church form", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p3RiknEI-G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Details tab: the Church Name, the Abbreviation (a short name, required and unique, used where the full name does not fit), the Legal Name (the registered name, for giving statements), the Image (a photo or logo), and the Address, Phone and Email in the Contact section. The Live Stream Link for the website's Watch Live page is there too (see the Website manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "M5YnfVfobp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- About tab: the About text for the website's About Us page, the Mission Statement, and the Church Verse (a Bible reference, such as John 3:16).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pFIgJnJ9Tk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Settings tab: the Tax ID for giving statements, the CCLI License Number for song slides, the Default Bible Translation, and Contact People Only With Their Consent (see Consent in the Communications manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Gmmalmy1c4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Where these details show:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1Rbu4LNCR6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Website: the About Us page uses the About and the Mission Statement. The footer and the Contact Us page use the address, phone and email. A blank phone or email uses Contact Us Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V47K0-O3Sy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Bulletin: the image on the front cover and the verse, with its words in your Default Bible Translation, on the back cover, when those sections are on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "luDqWact8q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Directory: the name, the Legal Name when it differs, the address, the website and the verse on the cover, and the image when Church Image on Cover is ticked.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QYXlaTjPqf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Giving statements: the Legal Name, the Tax ID and the address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qkU3D7WHls", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A branch church that leaves Legal Name, Tax ID, Default Bible Translation or Website blank uses its parent church's. Leave Legal Name and Tax ID blank on a branch when the main church is the registered charity that issues the receipts. The name, address and contact line on anything a branch prints are always its own.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VGpElOSOhv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Managers and System Managers change the Church record. Other staff read it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TpMGF1G4Bs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udfd8\ufe0fMore Than One Church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OvoNkktoBf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some organizations have more than one congregation: a main church with branch or satellite churches, or several campuses. Churchit can keep them in one site. Each church then has its own people, events, giving and settings, and each church's staff see only their own church's records, unless something is shared. People and families are the exception: by default every church can look them up (see One people directory).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4NxXKNcqxB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Grace Church has a main campus and a Downtown campus. The Downtown staff see Downtown's services, prayer requests and giving. The Downtown pastor can still look up any person, to welcome a visitor who usually goes to the main campus. The two campuses share one Building Fund and one Youth Retreat, so both can see and use them. Each campus's gifts to the fund stay in its own giving reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ezH3VwXZW6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turn it on", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Q5eM47fPFp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Church Features, open the Multi-Church section, read the warning under it, and tick Enable Multi-Church.
2. Open Churches and add each branch, with the main church as its Parent Church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "erxuAsS_-Q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you save a new branch, a message tells you what the branch needs next. The main church becomes a group when you add its first branch. There is always exactly one main church, the one with no parent.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5g07mVXPqV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turning Multi-Church on puts the main church on every existing record, and gives every existing user the main church with branches hidden, so nothing becomes visible to anyone by accident. You cannot turn it off again while branch churches exist. Without Multi-Church, only one Church record is allowed. The main church can never be deleted, and a church with branches cannot be deleted. Deleting a branch moves the users of that branch to its parent church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7tz-KNupPO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each record belongs to a church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Cs3Jcj9QhN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, each church-specific record, such as a Person, Family, Prayer Request, Function, Fund, Collection or Bulletin, gets a Church field. It shows near the top of the form, as a list filter and as a list column, which helps you tell apart records with the same name in two churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XT_lzEPsSP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- New records get the church of the person who saves them. A record that belongs to another record takes its church, such as a sign-up from its function, or a care request from its person. A family belongs to the church of its Primary Contact.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gKJGwMrSRB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- You can add such a record only for a record of your own church or a shared one. You cannot book another church's room, spend from its fund, or record a care request or a prayer for its people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AIuvTI5v1E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Single-church sites never see the Church field.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6070JrkQ2T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Share a record with every church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cP2PedW2L3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some records can be shared with every church: songs, sermons, sermon series and handouts, beliefs, question sets, vendors, rooms, locations, assets, functions, meeting minutes, funds and ministries. Each has a Shared with All Churches box. Sharing is one record at a time: nothing is shared until someone ticks the box on that record. A new Belief starts shared, because most branches share the main church's statement of faith. A branch that differs unticks it and writes its own.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gZgqVBovkH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Tick it, and every church can see and use the record. The Church field disappears, and Shared By names the church that shared it. Filter a list by Shared By to separate what you shared from what was shared with you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zKbXJ_G9aD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Only the church that shared a record can stop sharing it or delete it. Untick the box there, and the record goes back to that church, with anything attached to it, such as the bookings of a shared room. A branch that no longer wants something has to ask the church that shared it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lAZKjm7MYj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Anything attached to a shared record is shared too, such as a booking of a shared room or a sign-up for a shared function, so every church sees the same calendar and the same list of names.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "N91QN_Ob3p", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Gifts and expenses are never shared. Each keeps the church that gave or spent it, so every report shows a church only its own money. A shared fund shows its joint balance to every church that can see it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VavmuZMlpT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- People and attendance are never shared, but see One people directory below.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pLh8C4X38Q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Budget tracks the spending of its own church. Tick Include Branch Churches on it to count the spending of the churches beneath it too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZBJ6-3iHDi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Settings that every church shares", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3KgygmG4ED", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some settings serve every church: Church Features, People Settings, and the defaults in Giving Settings, Check-In Settings and Bulletin Settings. Only someone who works across every church (a user of the main church, or a user with no church) can change them. Branch staff see these pages as read-only, except for the rows of their own church under Payment Gateways, Wording Per Church, Printers Per Church and Sections Per Church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "43o9xD5-8S", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Lookups such as Member Status, Membership Type, Expense Type and Function Type are shared too. Only someone who works across every church can add or change one: a branch asks the main church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bKWBJjPRK7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What each church shows on the website, such as its own About text and photo on the Locations page, is in the Website manual. With more than one church, tick Publish on each church that should appear on the website.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JgXIGi4dn_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who sees which church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZT4JQ-QyiC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Everyone sees the records of their own church, and nothing of the others. Someone at a branch sees that branch's events, prayer requests and giving. The main church's records stay out of their way, and theirs stay out of the main church's.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tXnY0hxzac", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One people directory. People and families are the exception. Every church can look up every Person and Family, so a branch can find a visitor from the main church, choose a main-church pastor as a speaker, or check in a family from another campus.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NTEUJBNXTz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Only a person's own church can change them. Other churches see the form as read-only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FrujW_mU2T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Only a person's own church can add a Background Check, Care Request, Care Assignment or Visitation Log for them. A workflow that starts by itself, such as on a first check-in, still opens a follow-up card for a visitor from another church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3cpeiWQGnF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- To move someone to another church, use a Member Transfer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5IqXlh_bEN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Prayer, care, counseling, visits and giving stay with each church. While the directory is shared, finance and care staff of another church can see a person's Giving and Care figures in lists and reports, but not on the Person form, and Check-In, People Editor and Church Manager users of every church can read Medical Notes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CFCk49gx9H", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To keep each church's people and families, and those details, inside each church, tick Keep People and Families Private to Each Church in Church Features. The Check-In Station still finds everyone at a function shared with all churches. Church Manager, Church Staff and Church People Editor users of every church can still read addresses.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "c09kp5YpNG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which church a person sees", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iAheDBgZNn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members. A member sees the church in the Church field of their Person record. Fill that in, and give them a login (Actions, then Invite to Portal). There is nothing else to set up. If they move, change the same field, or confirm a Member Transfer with a To Church: what they can see moves with them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ze1ifqgQaN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Staff. A staff login that you add in the User list starts in your own church (the main church for Administrator). Linking it to a person by hand does not change that: the Person form then says under Portal User which church the login works in. To move it, someone who works across every church opens that Person and clicks Actions, then Limit Login to the person's church. A System Manager can also set a login's churches in User Permission.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Q2rn5SdXYx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For the manager of one branch, give the login the Church Branch Manager role profile, not Church Manager. Church Manager also changes the website, workspaces and shared reports, which affect every church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a0-p6PJFjO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One church only. Most people belong to one church. The app does not ask them to choose: the Church field and the Church filter are hidden for them, and what they create belongs to their church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "b4kkXzJfb0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "See the branches as well", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oJz1A5P2zG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Someone at a church with branches sees only their own church at first. To bring the branches in, choose Include Branch Churches in the user menu. While the branches are included:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XpNBRCXIh2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- a blue note sits at the top of every page, as a reminder,", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6InNsyvzaE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- the same menu item reads Hide Branch Churches, which puts things back,", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O08JyfTbFZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- lists and reports get a Church box: leave it empty to see every church, or pick one. Tick Expand filters to branches on the blue note to include the branches of the church you pick.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y7OqmZAfzy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who see everything. The built-in Administrator, and any user who has no church. Their reports still open on the main church: clear the Church box to see every church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-xAOhrd8fu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Assigning and sharing. With more than one church, you can assign a record (Assign To) or share it only with someone who can see that record's church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cZIB9xqqNL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If someone sees the wrong thing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RVohBow41q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Check the Church field on their Person record first. For a staff login, also read the note under Portal User on that Person. Behind the scenes Churchit keeps a User Permission for each login, which a System Manager can look at or change. A change made there by hand stays until the person's church or login changes: then Churchit sets it again from the Person record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Zc-rQxAmUd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Keep a church away from AI. Tick Keep This Church Away From AI on the Settings tab of a church to keep its records and people away from Churchit's AI features (see Keep a church or a person away from AI).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nAPCCjBicX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd4Beliefs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cgIxFrIVu-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Belief is one statement of what your church believes, such as \"Salvation by grace through faith\", with the Bible passages it rests on. Published beliefs make up the Beliefs page of your website.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4h1yq7Pgw0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qfs2yMHqNy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Beliefs and click Add Belief.
2. Type the Title and the Belief Statement. Each title must be unique.
3. Type the Bible References, such as Romans 3:23; Ephesians 2:8-9. They show under the statement on the website.
4. Tick Publish to show it on the website, and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nxMno-Ju9q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Beliefs list and page show the beliefs in the order you added them. A belief can also be a slide in a sermon presentation (see the Study manual). With more than one church, a new belief is shared with all churches (see Share a record with every church).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Sb59rWZrQa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc8Weekly Metrics", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6R8wcTp8Kw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Weekly Metrics keeps the numbers of each week, so you can see how the church is doing over time: attendance, first-time visitors, active members, people in groups, people who serve, and giving and givers. Churchit writes one record for each week (and for each church, with more than one) by itself every night. You find it in the Setup folder of the Summary sidebar.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7VGa36whmQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NN5ULcGCPS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
The elders want to know whether Easter brought lasting growth. They open Weekly Metrics and compare the attendance and the first-time visitors of the ten weeks after Easter with the same weeks of last year.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KpNsD4bHiK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each night, Churchit writes this week and counts last week again, so a late check-in or a late collection still counts. Members, groups and serving are counted on the day the record is written.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LMbwBhdhb2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you submit or cancel a collection of an older week, Churchit counts the giving of that week again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hX5zFEQz6Z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- You cannot add or change a record by hand. A Church Manager can delete one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EpuyVIRKA4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the numbers count. Attendance adds the attendance of each function that starts in the week. A function shared with all churches counts once, for the church that shared it. Giving adds every submitted collection of the week, the same total as the Weekly Giving chart, with sign-up and form payments. Givers counts each person who gave money in the week once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dHYp5xf-X8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see the giving numbers. The Summary workspace shows the Attendance by Week chart, the Giving by Week chart (for finance users and managers) and the Weekly Attendance card, which adds the attendance of this week's functions so far.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qutdIwfxIk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fill the past year. On a new site, Church Managers can click Fill the Last 52 Weeks on the Weekly Metrics list. It fills the attendance, first-time visitors and giving of the past weeks in the background: refresh the list in a few minutes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qB7hfYykV6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Past weeks show 0 for members, groups and serving, because Churchit cannot know those numbers for the past. A week that already has a record keeps its numbers. If you change the first day of the week in System Settings, the weeks around the change overlap.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xql4WazrGL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddeaSample Data", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p4QdPAgma-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Sample Data page fills the app with a made-up church, so you can try each part before you enter your own records. A Church Manager or a System Manager can open it, and only a System Manager can create or delete sample data.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tnt6maNCiv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zUMle-F1X2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Create Sample Data adds made-up people, families, funds and other records to your church, and demo logins that use their email address as the password.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rCodIRVTXy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Delete All Data removes the sample records and every record of those kinds that you added yourself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IzKYf5dAvj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Delete All Data
Delete All Data also deletes the records that you added yourself. Remove the sample data before the church starts to use the site. Do not use sample data on a site that people can reach from the internet, because each demo login has its email address as its password.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ywKJT1w5tB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd17Send records to other systems", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BB5grFEAah", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This part is for a System Manager. Churchit can send a record to another system when someone adds or changes it, for example to a mailing tool or a chat room, with no custom code.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Jc6lkdR8cY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Never send care, medical, pickup or giving fields to another system. The other system does not protect them as Churchit does, and it does not follow your church and consent rules.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eQXQwBPTp2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send a record with a Webhook", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xDBDFx4zZ4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Webhooks and add one:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AbHnMKBXrw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Set DocType to the record to send, such as Person or Connection Card, and Doc Event to when it goes, such as after_insert for a new record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FPMOg8kj_u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Set Request URL to the address that the other system gives you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "krcTGrgF-h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Tick Enable Security and type a Webhook Secret. Give the same secret to the other system, so that it can check that each request came from your site.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FcP4vj776T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Set Request Structure to JSON. In JSON Request Body, put only the fields that the other system needs, for example {\"first_name\": \"{{ doc.first_name }}\"}.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "d47ignCwnp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. With more than one church, type doc.church == \"CHURCH-ID\" in Condition, with the ID of the church. Then only that church's records go.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hYzP0_WhjC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A request that fails is kept in the Webhook Request Log.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WWukMDjeEL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send an alert to a chat room", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fa4ryrMWhJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe sends alerts to Slack, and Mattermost accepts the same alerts:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8dwWIA4ukr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the chat app, make an incoming webhook and copy its address.
2. Find Slack Webhook URL with the search bar, add one with a Name, and paste the address in Webhook URL.
3. Open Notifications and add one. Set Channel to Slack, choose the webhook in Slack Channel, and set Document Type, Send Alert On and Message.
4. With more than one church, type doc.church == \"CHURCH-ID\" in Condition.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gsAsGefB1i", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\udd16AI and your church's data", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w2oBHMBIT7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit can use AI (artificial intelligence) to help your staff: to draft an email, to summarize a report, to suggest the type of a new prayer request, or to answer \"who has not come in two months?\". AI is off until your church decides to turn it on. This part explains, in plain words, what AI can do with your church's data and how you stay in control. The second part, AI Setup for System Managers, has the technical steps.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "b1ySCb05aa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The most important points:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3cXSpn4bTQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- AI is off until you turn it on. While it is off, no AI feature of Churchit runs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IdXDmUx5bE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- AI works with a person's own permissions. An AI tool that a staff member uses can see and change exactly what that staff member can, and nothing more. So choose with care who may use AI.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2IAr_SmJRM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- AI only suggests. Churchit's AI features never save a record and never send a message. They give a draft or a suggestion, and a person reads it, changes it and saves it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qFpJkdPVwc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Private records need a private AI model. Records such as care requests, notes, visits and gifts go only to an AI model that keeps no copy of your data, or that runs on your own computer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "20FwwSh3_4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Anyone can stay out. A church or a person can ask Churchit's AI features to leave them out.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-Epa8X5bzx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- AI can be wrong. It can write something that looks right and is wrong, and it can miss a risk. Read everything it gives you.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zuPbwDmEyB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "There are three ways that AI can reach your church's data:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K7c0adlvkm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- AI apps, such as Claude or ChatGPT, that a staff member connects to the site.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sF9SW_x5H_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit's AI buttons in the desk, such as Brief Me or Draft with AI. The other manuals say where each one is.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "k2sroxRrgy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Flow, Frappe's AI agents, where a staff member chats with an AI in the desk. Flow comes with the next version of Frappe (Frappe 17), so a site on Frappe 16 does not have it yet. Churchit's AI buttons need Flow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_LRmrswC9O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example
Your church turns AI on and lets the pastor and the secretary use it. The secretary clicks Draft with AI on a Church Email and asks for a warm invitation to the picnic. The AI writes a draft into the form.
